mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the federal funds rate increased by more than 0.25% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in the last two months indicates a weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances where housing starts dropped by more than 5% in the previous two months.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending power diminishes.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the unemployment rate increased by more than 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the last two months signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic activity and corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where industrial production increased by more than 1% in the previous two months.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the last three months signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate revenues and earnings grow.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances where real personal consumption expenditures increased consistently over the previous three months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4.5% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the last month, it signals a tight labor market and strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.5% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the unemployment rate was below 4.5% and nonfarm payrolls increased by more than 200,000 in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% in the last month, it signals inflationary pressure and potential monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the federal funds rate was above 2% and the consumer price index increased by more than 0.3% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% in the last quarter signals a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and economic growth prospects diminish.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where GDP decreased by more than 0.5% in the previous quarter.
